binary_input.fix: Keep binary files out of the range and the patch; reviewed and patched files must be UTF-8 text without NUL bytes. For `apply`, also check the worktree copy of each target file, which is read before patching.
binary_input.summary: Text being screened or patched contains a NUL byte or isn't valid UTF-8, so it's treated as binary and refused.

blob_changed.fix: Run `git fsck` in the repository and retry once it reports no problems. If it repeats on a healthy repository, this indicates a bug; open an issue with the command and code, without private data.
blob_changed.summary: Git reported a different size for a stored file than the bytes it returned, so the read isn't trusted.

clean_worktree_required.fix: Commit, stash or remove the changes, including untracked files (ignored files and .finassist don't count), then rerun `finassist apply`. `verify-gate` reports the same reason when the worktree is dirty.
clean_worktree_required.summary: The worktree has uncommitted or untracked changes, so a patch can't be applied and readiness can't be confirmed.

decimal_limit_exceeded.fix: Use at most 200 characters, at most 18 decimal places and a magnitude below 10^31. Write values in plain notation; an exponent beyond 18 (such as 1E+19) is refused even when the value itself is in range.
decimal_limit_exceeded.summary: A numeric input is too long or outside the supported magnitude or precision, so exact checks can't use it.

empty_model_context.fix: Make sure at least one changed source file is inside `allow_paths` and not generated, then rebuild the packet with `finassist plan`. A range changing only generated or omitted files can't be model-reviewed.
empty_model_context.summary: The range changes files but the packet includes none for review, so there is nothing to send to the model.

empty_or_duplicate_patch.fix: Use a patch with at least one diff --git section and all hunks for each file in a single section. For a model proposal, rerun `finassist propose`; don't hand-edit an approved artifact.
empty_or_duplicate_patch.summary: The patch has no file sections, or names the same file in more than one section, so it can't be applied safely.

exact_decimal_required.fix: Write decimal amounts as JSON strings, such as "1234.56", or as integers. Floats, booleans and null are refused rather than rounded.
exact_decimal_required.summary: A numeric input is a JSON float or another non-numeric type, so its exact decimal value is unknown.

executable_mode_change_not_supported.fix: Apply mode-changing patches on Linux, macOS or WSL, or make the mode change with your project's explicit Git index workflow. Ordinary content-only patches apply normally here.
executable_mode_change_not_supported.summary: The patch changes a file mode or creates an executable file, which this platform can't represent in the worktree.

explicit_tax_method_required.fix: Set `method` in the input file to "separate-positive" or "offset-characters". The result is simplified arithmetic, not a jurisdiction's tax rules.
explicit_tax_method_required.summary: The tax check's `method` isn't one of the supported arithmetic methods, and no default is assumed.

explicit_timestamp_required.fix: Give `decision_time`, `published_at`, `retrieved_at`, `period_start` and `period_end` in ISO 8601 with an offset, such as "2026-03-31T00:00:00Z" or "+00:00". Date-only values are refused.
explicit_timestamp_required.summary: A timestamp is missing, not ISO 8601 or has no timezone, so point-in-time order can't be checked.

feature_branch_required.fix: Create a feature branch at the proposal's head (for example `git switch -c NAME`) and rerun `finassist apply` there. Protected names come from `protected_branches`; remote default branches are always excluded.
feature_branch_required.summary: The current branch is protected or is named like a remote's default branch, so patches aren't applied to it.

file_integrity_failed.fix: Don't edit or retry with the same packet; regenerate it with `finassist plan` for the same range and compare it with this one.
file_integrity_failed.summary: A file's content in the packet doesn't match its recorded hash, so the packet may have been altered.

file_limit_exceeded.fix: Raise `max_file_bytes` (up to 2,000,000; `fixture_max_file_bytes` for gate fixtures) or keep the file out of the range. The error's `limit` shows the cap; 128000 and 4096 are fixed caps on policy, profile, ignore and marker files.
file_limit_exceeded.summary: A file version is larger than the byte limit that applies to it, so it can't be read or reviewed.

finding_evidence_invalid.fix: For a model review, rerun `finassist review` (a new paid request) or try another model. For `verify-gate`, pass the review report produced from this exact packet, unedited.
finding_evidence_invalid.summary: A review finding cites evidence that doesn't match the packet's files, hashes or line ranges.

finding_line_invalid.fix: For a model review, rerun `finassist review` (a new paid request) or try another model. For `verify-gate`, pass the review report produced from this exact packet, unedited.
finding_line_invalid.summary: A review finding points at a line beyond the end of the cited file version, so its source reference is invalid.

finding_outside_scope.fix: For a model review, rerun `finassist review` (a new paid request) or try another model. For `verify-gate`, pass the review report produced from this exact packet, unedited.
finding_outside_scope.summary: A review finding names a file that isn't in the reviewed packet, so it can't be source-checked.

fixture_marker_path_invalid.fix: This indicates a bug; open an issue with the command and code, without private data.
fixture_marker_path_invalid.summary: An internal fixture-marker read used a path that isn't a marker file; users can't cause this.

fixture_root_contains_data.fix: Move synthetic fixtures out of any directory named data (in any case) and update `fixture_roots` in the base policy. Real data stays out of review.
fixture_root_contains_data.summary: A fixture root or fixture file has a `data` path component, which is always private and never reviewed.

fixture_root_invalid.fix: List each root in `fixture_roots` as a literal file or directory prefix without *, ?, [ or ], and spell tests and fixtures components exactly in lowercase.
fixture_root_invalid.summary: A fixture root uses a wildcard, or a path uses a case variant of tests/fixtures, so it isn't a valid literal root.

fixture_root_unqualified.fix: Commit a .finledgerpoli-synthetic file in that directory (or beside the listed file) on the base branch, UTF-8, with the first line exactly `synthetic: true`, or move the fixtures under a tests or fixtures directory.
fixture_root_unqualified.summary: A fixture root outside tests/ or fixtures/ has no valid synthetic marker at the policy base.

forbidden_token_configuration_changed.fix: Keep the token file unchanged while a gate or history run is in progress (even an equivalent rewrite counts), then start the run again. If nothing should have touched it, find out what did.
forbidden_token_configuration_changed.summary: The forbidden-token list changed during the run, so earlier screening no longer applies and the request stops.

forbidden_token_file_invalid.fix: Point `forbidden_token_file` at an absolute regular file outside every checkout of the repository, not linked, with one numeric literal per line: UTF-8, no BOM or blank lines, at most 1,024 lines and 128 KiB.
forbidden_token_file_invalid.summary: The forbidden-token file can't be used: wrong location, not a plain private file, or its lines aren't valid numbers.

forbidden_token_hashes_invalid.fix: List each hash as 64 lowercase hex characters, the SHA256 of the canonical numeric string in UTF-8, with at most 1,024 entries.
forbidden_token_hashes_invalid.summary: `forbidden_token_hashes` isn't a list of at most 1,024 lowercase 64-character SHA256 hex strings.

forbidden_token_invalid.fix: Use plain numbers: dot decimals, one consistent thousands separator, an optional sign, parentheses or currency prefix, and at most 128 digits. In a token file this is reported as forbidden_token_file_invalid.
forbidden_token_invalid.summary: A value isn't a supported numeric literal for confidential-figure normalization.

forbidden_token_present.fix: Remove the figure from the changed files, or keep those files out of the range. Both file versions are screened, including context and comments. Very short listed numbers can match ordinary constants.
forbidden_token_present.summary: Source, instructions or model output contain a figure on the policy's confidential list, so the gate blocks.

gate_ignore_check_unavailable.fix: Check that Git works in the repository and that `git check-ignore` runs there without error (a valid repository and readable .gitignore files), then rerun the gate.
gate_ignore_check_unavailable.summary: Git couldn't evaluate ignore rules for the changed paths, so the gate can't confirm none of them are ignored.

gate_private_path.fix: Keep these files out of the reviewed range. Names such as client.json or secrets.json, names containing client_config or household_settings, and paths over 512 characters are also refused; there is no override.
gate_private_path.summary: The path has a private component or name (such as data, private, client or household), so it's never sent for review.

generated_omission_invalid.fix: Don't edit packets. Rebuild it with `finassist plan` for the same range under the configuration you review with, and compare it with this one.
generated_omission_invalid.summary: The packet marks a file as a generated-artifact omission, but it isn't under the configured `generated_paths`.

generated_source_in_packet.fix: Don't edit packets. Rebuild it with `finassist plan` for the same range under the configuration you review with, and compare it with this one.
generated_source_in_packet.summary: The packet includes content from a file under `generated_paths`, which should appear only as an omission.

git_capability_check_failed.fix: Check that a working native Git is first on PATH (`git --version` should succeed) and reinstall or update it if not, then rerun.
git_capability_check_failed.summary: Running `git --no-lazy-fetch --version` failed, so the tool can't confirm how to keep Git offline.

git_commit_unavailable.fix: Fetch the branch or commit yourself (for example `git fetch origin BRANCH`) and pass a revision that `git rev-parse` resolves locally, then rerun.
git_commit_unavailable.summary: A requested commit isn't in the local repository, and the tool never fetches it.

git_newline_policy_invalid.fix: Set core.autocrlf to true, false or input and core.eol to lf, crlf or native (or unset them), and check that your Git config files parse with `git config --list`.
git_newline_policy_invalid.summary: Git's core.autocrlf or core.eol setting has an unsupported value or couldn't be read, so newline handling is unknown.

git_newline_policy_unavailable.fix: Check that Git is on PATH and answers `git config --get core.autocrlf` within 10 seconds, and that core.autocrlf and core.eol hold plain ASCII values.
git_newline_policy_unavailable.summary: Git couldn't be run to read the newline settings, or returned non-ASCII output, so status and apply stop.

git_partial_clone_unsupported.fix: Upgrade Git to 2.45 or later, or use a complete local clone without promisor or partial-clone settings. The tool won't fetch objects or change Git configuration for you.
git_partial_clone_unsupported.summary: The repository is a partial clone and this Git is older than 2.45, so missing objects could be fetched silently.

git_read_failed.fix: Check that `--repo` is a Git checkout, `git status` works there and path names are UTF-8; each Git call has a 30-second limit. For `apply`, check out a branch: a detached HEAD fails here.
git_read_failed.summary: A Git command failed, timed out or returned non-UTF-8 output, so the repository couldn't be read.

incomplete_patch_reconciliation_required.fix: Inspect the backups under .finassist: compare the files with the backup lacking a valid receipt, restore by hand if needed, then move that reconciled backup aside before applying again.
incomplete_patch_reconciliation_required.summary: A saved patch backup has no valid receipt, so an earlier apply may have been interrupted.

invalid_decimal.fix: Use a plain decimal string such as "-1234.56": digits with an optional sign and decimal point, without thousands separators, currency symbols or units.
invalid_decimal.summary: A numeric input string isn't a decimal number, so the exact check can't read it.

invalid_evidence_policy.fix: Set `max_age_days` to a nonnegative JSON integer (default 90) and `require_approved` to true or false, or omit both to use the defaults.
invalid_evidence_policy.summary: The observation check's `max_age_days` or `require_approved` has the wrong type or a negative value.

invalid_fixture_limit.fix: Set `fixture_max_file_bytes` in the policy to a whole number from 1 to 2,000,000 written without a decimal point, or omit it to use 48,000.
invalid_fixture_limit.summary: `fixture_max_file_bytes` isn't an integer from 1 to 2,000,000, so the fixture size limit is undefined.

invalid_patch_hash.fix: Pass the `patch_hash` printed by `finassist apply` (the proposal's approval hash) to `finassist rollback --patch-hash`.
invalid_patch_hash.summary: `--patch-hash` isn't 64 lowercase hex characters, so no patch backup can be selected.

invalid_provider_key.fix: Set the variable named by `api_key_env` again without carriage returns or line feeds; a trailing newline from reading a file is a common cause. Never paste the key into config or issues.
invalid_provider_key.summary: The API key variable's value contains a line break, which can't be sent safely in an HTTP header.

invalid_provider_response.fix: Check that `provider` matches the endpoint's API (for example `compatible` for Chat Completions-style services) and that `model` is valid. Record the actual charge for the open reservation with `finassist reconcile-budget` before retrying.
invalid_provider_response.summary: The provider returned JSON without the fields expected for the configured `provider`, so no output was accepted.

invalid_rate.fix: Give `short_rate` and `long_rate` as fractions between 0 and 1, such as "0.37" for 37 percent, written as strings or integers.
invalid_rate.summary: A tax rate is outside 0 to 1, so the estimate would be meaningless.

invalid_revision.fix: Pass a commit hash, branch or tag that exists in this repository to `--base` or `--head`. Option-like values beginning with '-' are refused.
invalid_revision.summary: A revision argument is empty, starts with '-', or didn't resolve to a full commit hash.

invalid_tolerance.fix: Set `tolerance` to zero or a positive decimal string such as "0.01", or omit it to require an exact match.
invalid_tolerance.summary: The cash check's `tolerance` is negative, so the comparison is meaningless.

invalid_weight_check.fix: Provide at least one value in `weights` and a nonnegative `tolerance` (default "0.000001"), with values as decimal strings or integers.
invalid_weight_check.summary: The weights check has an empty `weights` list or a negative `tolerance`.

linked_path.fix: Use locations without links for the repository, input, output and state paths. Linked files inside a repository are refused rather than followed; keep them out of the change.
linked_path.summary: A path or one of its parent directories is a symbolic link, junction or reparse point; links are never followed.

non_text_publication_file.fix: Make sure the file is meant to be published. Convert it to UTF-8 text, or remove it from the tracked files.
non_text_publication_file.summary: The publication scan found a tracked file that isn't UTF-8 text, so it couldn't be screened.

nonfinite_decimal.fix: Replace it with a finite decimal string. Report missing values as missing rather than as NaN or Infinity.
nonfinite_decimal.summary: A numeric input is NaN or infinite, so it can't be used in an exact check.

observation_fields_missing.fix: Include entity, metric, value, unit, period_start, period_end, published_at, retrieved_at, source, status and period_kind in `observation` (`evidence add` sets status itself).
observation_fields_missing.summary: The observation lacks one or more required fields, so its point-in-time validity can't be checked.

packet_allow_paths_mismatch.fix: Run with the same `--config` used for `finassist plan`, or rebuild the packet with `finassist plan` under the current configuration and approve the new one.
packet_allow_paths_mismatch.summary: The packet was built with different `allow_paths` than the current configuration, so its scope doesn't match.

packet_allow_paths_missing.fix: Rebuild the packet with `finassist plan` using the current version and configuration, then inspect and approve the new packet.
packet_allow_paths_missing.summary: The packet has no recorded `allow_paths`, typically because an older version built it, so scope can't be verified.

packet_approval_required.fix: Inspect the packet, then pass its `packet_hash` (printed by `finassist plan`) to `--approve-packet`. A packet changed after you inspected it needs a fresh inspection.
packet_approval_required.summary: `--approve-packet` is missing or doesn't equal the packet's hash, so no model request is sent.

packet_coverage_invalid.fix: Don't edit packets. Rebuild it with `finassist plan` for the same range under the configuration you review with, and compare it with this one.
packet_coverage_invalid.summary: The packet's changed paths aren't each accounted for exactly once by its files and omissions.

packet_file_count_limit.fix: Review a smaller range: choose a closer `--base` or split the change into several ranges, and build a packet for each with `finassist plan`.
packet_file_count_limit.summary: The packet lists more than 2,000 changed paths, more than one packet may carry.

packet_generated_paths_mismatch.fix: Run with the same `--config` used for `finassist plan`, or rebuild the packet with `finassist plan` under the current configuration and approve the new one.
packet_generated_paths_mismatch.summary: The packet was built with different `generated_paths` than the current configuration.

packet_integrity_failed.fix: Don't edit or retry with the same packet; regenerate it with `finassist plan` for the same range, compare it with this one, and approve the new hash.
packet_integrity_failed.summary: The packet's contents don't match its `packet_hash`, so it may have been edited after it was built.

packet_limit_exceeded.fix: Raise `max_packet_bytes` (up to 2,000,000), narrow `allow_paths` or plan a smaller range. A packet built under a larger limit is refused by a config with a smaller one; in a policy gate the cap is fixed.
packet_limit_exceeded.summary: The serialized packet is larger than `max_packet_bytes`, so it can't be built or sent.

packet_mode_invalid.fix: Don't edit packets. Rebuild it with `finassist plan` for the same range under the configuration you review with, and compare it with this one.
packet_mode_invalid.summary: A packet file record has a mode other than 100644 or 100755, or a mode on a missing side.

packet_outside_allowlist.fix: Don't edit packets. Rebuild it with `finassist plan` for the same range under the configuration you review with, and compare it with this one.
packet_outside_allowlist.summary: The packet includes a file outside the configured `allow_paths`, so it doesn't match this policy.

packet_profile_mismatch.fix: Run with the same `--config` used for `finassist plan`, or rebuild the packet with `finassist plan` under the current configuration and approve the new one.
packet_profile_mismatch.summary: The packet was built for a different `profile` than the current configuration selects.

packet_schema_invalid.fix: Pass the packet file written by `finassist plan --output`, not a review, proposal or edited copy. If it did come from plan, regenerate it and compare.
packet_schema_invalid.summary: The input isn't a valid packet: its keys, schema version, hashes or file records don't match the packet format.

patch_apply_failed_inspect_backup.fix: Don't retry. Compare the files with the backup under .finassist (named by the approval hash) and `git status`, restore by hand if needed, then reconcile the backup before another apply.
patch_apply_failed_inspect_backup.summary: Git failed while applying the patch after the backup was saved, so the worktree may be partly changed.

patch_approval_mismatch.fix: Pass the proposal's `approval_hash` to `--approve-hash`. If it already matches, the artifact changed after approval: don't edit or retry it; regenerate with `finassist propose` and compare.
patch_approval_mismatch.summary: The proposal artifact's hash doesn't equal `--approve-hash`, so it isn't the artifact you approved.

patch_artifact_invalid.fix: Pass the proposal file written by `finassist propose --output` unchanged; `apply` reads its `artifact` object. Don't build or edit artifacts by hand.
patch_artifact_invalid.summary: The proposal artifact doesn't have exactly the string fields head, patch and summary.

patch_backup_integrity_failed.fix: Don't edit or retry with these files; keep them for inspection. Apply never commits, so you can usually restore the patched files from HEAD with `git restore` after saving any later work.
patch_backup_integrity_failed.summary: A patch backup and its receipt don't match each other, so rollback won't trust them.

patch_backup_unavailable.fix: Check the hash and that .finassist still holds both the backup and its receipt. If apply was interrupted before writing the receipt, restore the files by hand from the backup.
patch_backup_unavailable.summary: The backup or receipt for this patch hash is missing or unreadable, so rollback can't proceed.

patch_does_not_apply.fix: Rebuild the packet for the current head with `finassist plan` and request a new proposal. Trailing spaces, blank lines added at end of file and spaces before tabs are refused.
patch_does_not_apply.summary: The patch doesn't apply cleanly to the reviewed or current files, for example due to context or whitespace errors.

patch_format_not_supported.fix: Use a plain text diff with only diff --git, index, ---/+++ and @@ hunk lines per file. Make renames and binary changes by hand; for a model proposal, rerun `finassist propose`.
patch_format_not_supported.summary: The patch uses an unsupported form, such as a rename, copy, binary change or an unrecognized header line.

patch_head_changed.fix: Check out the proposal's head on a feature branch, or build a new packet for the current HEAD with `finassist plan` and request a new proposal.
patch_head_changed.summary: The repository HEAD isn't the commit the proposal was made for, so the patch could target the wrong code.

patch_header_mismatch.fix: Each section needs a --- a/PATH and +++ b/PATH pair (or /dev/null) for the same path before its hunks. For a model proposal, rerun `finassist propose`; don't hand-edit an approved artifact.
patch_header_mismatch.summary: A file section's ---/+++ headers are missing, repeated, out of order or don't match its diff --git path.

patch_hunk_invalid.fix: Each @@ header's counts must match its context, added and removed lines, each starting with a space, + or -. For a model proposal, rerun `finassist propose`; don't hand-edit an approved artifact.
patch_hunk_invalid.summary: A hunk header is malformed or its line counts don't match the lines that follow.

patch_invalid.fix: Check that the patch is a valid Git diff with UTF-8 path names and that Git works in this repository. Don't edit an approved artifact; regenerate it with `finassist propose`.
patch_invalid.summary: Git couldn't parse the patch or list the files it changes, so it isn't applied.

patch_limit_exceeded.fix: Raise `max_packet_bytes` (up to 2,000,000) or request a smaller patch that fixes fewer issues at once.
patch_limit_exceeded.summary: The patch is larger than `max_packet_bytes`, so it isn't processed.

patch_not_applied.fix: No rollback is needed if it was already rolled back; check the files with `git status`. Each applied patch can be rolled back once, by its `patch_hash`.
patch_not_applied.summary: The receipt for this patch isn't in the applied state, typically because it was already rolled back.

patch_path_not_approved.fix: Make changes to protected or unlisted files yourself through normal review. Adjust `allow_paths` or `protected_paths` only through reviewed configuration, then regenerate the proposal.
patch_path_not_approved.summary: The patch changes a file outside `allow_paths` or inside `protected_paths`, so it can't be proposed or applied.

patch_rename_or_path_invalid.fix: Use one section per file with the same path on both sides and no whitespace in the path. Make renames by hand; for a model proposal, rerun `finassist propose`.
patch_rename_or_path_invalid.summary: A diff --git line names different old and new paths, or a path containing spaces, which isn't supported.

patch_scope_mismatch.fix: Don't edit or retry with the same artifact; regenerate the proposal with `finassist propose` and compare the patches.
patch_scope_mismatch.summary: Git and finassist disagree on which files the patch changes, so it's refused as ambiguous.

patch_special_file.fix: Limit the patch to regular files with mode 100644 or 100755. Make link or submodule changes by hand through normal review.
patch_special_file.summary: The patch creates or changes a symbolic link, submodule or other special file; only regular files are patched.

patch_target_not_regular.fix: Resolve that path in the worktree first, for example by moving aside a stray directory with that name, then rerun `finassist apply`.
patch_target_not_regular.summary: A file the patch writes exists in the worktree as a directory or special file, not a regular file.

pinned_runner_image_required.fix: Set `runner_image` to the image id `sha256:` plus 64 hex characters, or NAME@sha256: plus the digest. Tags such as :latest are refused; build and inspect the image first.
pinned_runner_image_required.summary: `runner_image` isn't pinned to a sha256 digest, so the test environment isn't immutable.

policy_request_approval_invalid.fix: This indicates a bug; open an issue with the command and code, without private data.
policy_request_approval_invalid.summary: An internal policy approval record isn't made of two SHA256 hashes; users can't cause this.

private_or_binary_path.fix: Keep such files out of the range; a changed one blocks planning even outside `allow_paths`. Only a synthetic .csv or .tsv fixture can be admitted, through `fixture_roots` in a reviewed gate policy.
private_or_binary_path.summary: The path has a data, credential or binary suffix (such as .csv, .pdf, .zip or .key), which is never reviewed.

private_path.fix: Keep the file out of the range; a changed private path blocks planning even outside `allow_paths`. Approved source can be admitted by removing its component from `denied_parts`; .git, .finassist and .env names always stay private.
private_path.summary: A path component is private by policy (such as .git, .env, .ssh, secrets, holdings or node_modules), so it's never reviewed.

private_profile_path.fix: Keep these files out of the range. If it is ordinary documentation that happens to use one of these names, rename it before planning.
private_profile_path.summary: A file named auth.json, user.md, memory.md or session.md (any case) is treated as private agent state and never reviewed.

private_state_tracked.fix: Stop tracking it with `git rm -r --cached .finassist`, add .finassist/ to .gitignore and commit, then check history for anything private before publishing.
private_state_tracked.summary: Files under .finassist are tracked by Git, but that directory holds private local state.

profile_mismatch.fix: Run with the same `--config` used for `finassist plan`, or rebuild the packet with `finassist plan` under the current configuration and approve the new one.
profile_mismatch.summary: The configured `profile` differs from the packet's profile, so the review instructions wouldn't match.

project_content_blocked.fix: Remove the matching text from the files in the range. If a project pattern is broader than intended, narrow it through your reviewed configuration; built-in screening still applies.
project_content_blocked.summary: Text matched one of the project's `extra_sensitive_patterns`, so it's blocked from review or output.

proposal_head_mismatch.fix: Rerun `finassist propose` (a new paid request) or try another model; check `finassist audit` for any unsettled reservation first.
proposal_head_mismatch.summary: The model's proposal names a different head commit than the packet, so it can't be trusted for this source.

proposal_outside_review_scope.fix: Rerun `finassist propose`, or if those files belong in scope, widen the range or `allow_paths`, rebuild the packet with `finassist plan` and approve it again.
proposal_outside_review_scope.summary: The proposed patch edits files that weren't included in the reviewed packet.

proposal_schema_invalid.fix: Rerun `finassist propose` or try another model; raising `max_output_tokens` can help if output was cut short. Check `finassist audit` for any unsettled reservation first.
proposal_schema_invalid.summary: The model's proposal isn't JSON with exactly head, patch and summary, or exceeds their size limits.

provider_deadline_exceeded.fix: Raise `timeout_seconds` or send a smaller packet. The provider may still bill: Record the actual charge for the open reservation with `finassist reconcile-budget` before retrying.
provider_deadline_exceeded.summary: The provider's response took longer than `timeout_seconds` to stream, so it was abandoned.

provider_empty_output.fix: Check that `model` supports this request and that `max_output_tokens` leaves room for an answer, then retry. Record the actual charge for the open reservation with `finassist reconcile-budget` before retrying.
provider_empty_output.summary: The provider reported success but returned no text, so there is nothing to validate.

provider_http_error.fix: Check `endpoint`, `model`, key permissions, quota and provider status. Find the open reservation with `finassist audit` and record the provider's actual charge with `finassist reconcile-budget` before retrying.
provider_http_error.summary: The provider returned a non-200 HTTP status; the response body is never shown because it may echo input.

provider_incomplete.fix: Raise `max_output_tokens` or send a smaller packet, then retry. Record the actual charge for the open reservation with `finassist reconcile-budget` before retrying.
provider_incomplete.summary: The provider reported the response as unfinished, for example cut off by the token limit or stopped early.

provider_key_missing.fix: Set the variable named by `api_key_env` (built-in defaults: OPENAI_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, GEMINI_API_KEY) in this shell. Never put the key itself in a config or policy file.
provider_key_missing.summary: The environment variable named for the provider key is unset or empty, so no request is sent.

provider_not_remote.fix: Set `provider` and `model` in your configuration to a remote or local model provider to use `finassist propose`. Offline mode supports planning and offline review only.
provider_not_remote.summary: The configured provider is `offline`, so there is no model to call for this command.

provider_response_limit.fix: Lower `max_output_tokens` or send a smaller packet, and check that `endpoint` is the intended API. Record the actual charge for the open reservation with `finassist reconcile-budget` before retrying.
provider_response_limit.summary: The provider's response exceeded the fixed 2,000,000-byte limit, so it was discarded.

provider_transport_failed.fix: Check network access, `endpoint`, TLS and `timeout_seconds`. The provider may have processed it: check its usage and record the charge with `finassist reconcile-budget` before retrying.
provider_transport_failed.summary: The request failed in transport (connection, TLS, timeout or a non-JSON body), so its outcome is unknown.

provider_usage_exceeds_limit.fix: Check the provider's billing for the actual charge and record it with `finassist reconcile-budget`. Then review `max_output_tokens`, `max_run_usd` and your price settings before retrying.
provider_usage_exceeds_limit.summary: Reported usage or cost exceeds `max_output_tokens`, the input estimate or `max_run_usd`, so it stays unreconciled.

public_image_hash_mismatch.fix: Don't just update the hash. Inspect the image for private content first; only after review, record its new SHA256 in the manifest and rerun `finassist scan`.
public_image_hash_mismatch.summary: A catalogued image's bytes don't match the SHA256 recorded in the image manifest.

public_image_invalid.fix: Re-export it as a standard PNG of at most 4096 x 4096 pixels, with IHDR first, at least one IDAT and IEND last, then update its manifest hash after review.
public_image_invalid.summary: A catalogued PNG has a broken structure, misplaced chunks or dimensions outside 1 to 4096 pixels.

public_image_manifest_invalid.fix: Give the manifest only `schema_version` 1 and `images`, mapping at most 32 tracked images in the supported locations to 64-character lowercase SHA256 hashes, in under 64,000 bytes.
public_image_manifest_invalid.summary: The image manifest isn't valid: wrong size, keys or version, too many entries, or an unsupported path or bad hash.

public_image_metadata_or_format_invalid.fix: Re-export PNGs with only IHDR, IDAT and IEND chunks (no text, color-profile or palette chunks). The GIF needs 2 to 300 frames under 15 seconds in total, with only loop and frame-delay extensions.
public_image_metadata_or_format_invalid.summary: A catalogued image has metadata or unsupported structure, such as extra PNG chunks, a bad CRC or GIF extensions.

public_image_too_large.fix: Reduce the image's dimensions, frame count or file size, review it again and update its manifest hash.
public_image_too_large.summary: A catalogued image is over its size cap (2,000,000 bytes for PNG, under 3,000,000 for the GIF) or isn't a regular file.

publication_file_too_large.fix: Shrink or split the file, or move it out of the published tree.
publication_file_too_large.summary: The publication scan found a tracked file over its 2,000,000-byte limit, so it wasn't screened.

remote_default_invalid.fix: Repair it with `git remote set-head NAME BRANCH`, naming the remote's real default branch, or remove it with `git remote set-head NAME -d`, then rerun `finassist apply`.
remote_default_invalid.summary: A remote's HEAD reference points outside that remote's namespace, so its default branch can't be identified.

request_approval_mismatch.fix: Rerun the gate from the start, keeping the configuration and provider key variable unchanged during the run. If it repeats, this indicates a bug; open an issue with the command and code, without private data.
request_approval_mismatch.summary: The outgoing request changed after it was approved, so it isn't sent.

review_coverage_mismatch.fix: For a model review, rerun `finassist review` (a new paid request) or try another model. For `verify-gate`, pass the review report produced from this exact packet, unedited.
review_coverage_mismatch.summary: The review's `reviewed_paths` don't list exactly the files in the packet, so coverage is unproven.

review_head_mismatch.fix: For a model review, rerun `finassist review` (a new paid request) or try another model. For `verify-gate`, pass the review report produced from this exact packet, unedited.
review_head_mismatch.summary: The review names a different head commit than the packet, so it doesn't describe this source.

review_schema_invalid.fix: For a model review, rerun `finassist review` or try another model; raise `max_output_tokens` if output was cut. For `verify-gate`, pass the full report written by `finassist review --output`.
review_schema_invalid.summary: The review document doesn't match the review schema, so its findings can't be validated.

rollback_head_changed.fix: Check out the commit the patch was applied at to roll back, or undo a committed change with ordinary Git, such as `git revert`.
rollback_head_changed.summary: HEAD has moved since the patch was applied, so rollback can't confirm the files it would restore.

rollback_outside_active_policy.fix: Run rollback with the same `--config` used for apply, or restore those files by hand from the backup through normal review.
rollback_outside_active_policy.summary: Under the current configuration a backed-up file is outside `allow_paths` or inside `protected_paths`.

rollback_would_overwrite_later_work.fix: Save or undo the later edits so the files match the post-apply state, then rerun rollback, or restore the original content by hand from the backup.
rollback_would_overwrite_later_work.summary: A patched file changed after apply, so rolling back would discard that later work.

scope_not_approved.fix: Rebuild the packet with `finassist plan` under the configuration you review with; don't edit packets.
scope_not_approved.summary: A packet file is outside the configured `allow_paths`, so the model call is refused.

sensitive_content.fix: Remove the secret or identifier from the file, rotate any real credential, and refer to keys only by environment variable name. Both versions of a changed file are screened; screening has no bypass.
sensitive_content.summary: Text matched a built-in credential or private-identifier pattern, so it's blocked from review, output or config.

unsupported_file_type.fix: If it is text source, add its suffix to `text_suffixes` in your configuration (for example .tf), or keep it out of `allow_paths`. In a policy gate, every changed file needs a supported suffix.
unsupported_file_type.summary: The file's suffix isn't in `text_suffixes`, so it isn't treated as reviewable source.
